attachments.landmark_b: head, neck and tubercle of the rib

bands.name: Radiate ligament of the head of the rib

attachments.landmark_a: anterior aspect of the head of the rib
attachments.landmark_b: bodies of the two adjacent vertebrae and the intervening disc

bands.mechanical_role: binds the rib head to the vertebral column
bands.function_note: Its three fan-shaped bands are why the rib head is anchored to two vertebrae rather than one.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Intra-articular ligament of the head of the rib
bands.mechanical_role: divides the costovertebral joint into two synovial compartments
bands.function_note: Absent for ribs 1, 10, 11 and 12, whose heads articulate with a single vertebra.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Costotransverse ligament

attachments.landmark_b: transverse process of the corresponding vertebra

bands.mechanical_role: binds the rib neck to the transverse process
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Superior costotransverse ligament

attachments.landmark_a: crest of the neck of the rib
attachments.landmark_b: transverse process of the vertebra above

bands.function_note: Its lateral border helps bound the space through which the thoracic paravertebral block is placed.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

function: Bind each rib to the vertebral column at two points -- head and tubercle -- which together define the fixed axis about which the rib rotates in respiration. The orientation of that axis, more transverse above and more sagittal below, is what makes the upper ribs move in pump-handle and the lower in bucket-handle fashion.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
